title_original: UK-Ireland box office preview: ‘Focker In-Law’, ‘Hexed’ lead new releases
excerpt_original: David Fincher’s ‘The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth’ gets Imax release for Netflix.

blocks.text: Source: Paramount / Disney
‘Focker In-Law’, ‘Hexed’
Paramount comedy Focker In-Law is the widest new release in UK and Ireland cinemas this weekend as Disney’s Hexed and Netflix’s The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth are also out.
Focker In-Law is opening in 624 locations for Paramount. It is the fourth instalment in the family-themed comedy series starring Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro.

The first film, Meet The Parents , came out 26 years ago with a £2.3m debut and a total of £15.5m across its run. Five years later, Meet The Fockers nearly doubled that – opening on £7.9m for a £28.9m cume. The third entry, 2010’s Little Fockers , landed somewhere in between with a £3m opening and a £19.2m cume.

De Niro and Stiller return for Focker In-Law alongside Ariana Grande who plays the newest in-law shaking up family dynamics. Skyler Gisondo, Beanie Feldstein and Eduardo Franco also star. It is directed by John Hamburg.
Disney is launching its latest animated feature Hexed in 595 sites. The film centres on a teenage girl who discovers magical abilities that transport her and her mother into a witch realm.

Disney’s original animations – non-sequel or Pixar titles – have struggled post-pandemic. The most successful of these originals is 2023’s Wish , debuting on £2.4m for a £13.2m cume, but before that was 2022’s Strange World (£830,000 debut; £4.1m cume) and 2021’s Covid-impacted Encanto (£1.7m debut; £9m cume).
Cliff Booth returns
In event titles, Trafalgar Releasing is screening Andrew Lloyd Webber’s Starlight Express in 486 cinemas from Thursday (November 26) while CinemaLive has Doctor Who - The Satan Pit in 276 cinemas.

Horror film Buddy is opening in 172 locations for Vertigo Releasing. The Sundance premiere follows a group of children trapped inside a Barney & Friends -style TV show who must find a way to escape the terrifying unicorn host. Casper Kelly directs with a cast including Cristin Milioti, Topher Grace, Patton Oswalt and Keegan-Michael Key.
Indian romance Yeh Prem Mol Liya debuts in 123 cinemas via Yash Raj Films.

Sony is opening US action film Ghost Soldier in 107 venues. Directed by William Eubank, the film follows a former special-ops soldier (Jim Caviezel) who wages war when a ruthless corporation tries to size his hometown.

France’s Oscar entry Minotaur is out in 59 sites via Mubi. Andrey Zvyagintsev’s crime drama is set in Russia 2022 as a businessman discovers his wife has been unfaithful. The film won the Grand Prix in Cannes and is nominated for two European Film Awards and three Gothams.

blocks.alt: The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth

blocks.text: Source: Netflix
‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’

Netflix has three films on release this weekend with David Fincher’s The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth getting an exclusive two-week Imax run in approximately 20-25 sites before regular screenings from December 11.

links.text: The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth

blocks.text: It is a sequel to Quentin Tarantino’s Once Upon A Time In… Hollywood which debuted with £7.6m in 2019 for a £21.5m cume. Tarantino penned the screenplay for Cliff Booth , set eight years after the events of the first film, which also sees the return of Brad Pitt in the titular role. Further cast includes Elizabeth Debicki, Peter Weller, Yahya Abdul-Mateen II and Scott Caan.
Netflix also has awards-qualifying runs for animated romance In Waves and Ava DuVernay documentary 14 th , which explores the US Constitution’s 14 th amendment regarding equal rights.

Korean coming-of-age drama The World Of A Love opens in four venues for Bulldog Film Distribution. Directed by Yoon Ga-eun, the Toronto premiere follows a 17-year-old girl whose world is turned upside down when she refuses to participate in a school-wide petition.

Sundance award-winning documentary To Hold A Mountain is out in two cinemas via MetFilm Distribution. Set in the remote highlands of Montenegro, the film centres on a mother and daughter who defend their ancestral land from Nato military training threats.

Further releases include Palestinian documentary Who Is Still Alive via Akka Films; Israeli drama Tell Me Everything ; Spanish documentary The Boy And The Suit Of Lights via Aconite Productions; and New Zealand-set drama Big Girls Don’t Cry via Peccadillo Pictures.
